capture.text:
ABOUT GENESIS

We are a full-stack general-purpose robot company, born across San Francisco and Paris and bound by a single mission: to make general-purpose robots a reality, unlocking infinite physical labor for the world and freeing people for creativity, exploration, and the pursuits they love for their own sake.

We are French and American by birth and global by nature. We are backed by partners who share our vision, including Eclipse, Khosla Ventures, Bpifrance, and HSG, alongside Eric Schmidt, Xavier Niel, Daniela Rus, and Vladlen Koltun. Our people work across the Bay Area and Europe, building the engine that will teach robots to do real work in the real world. We recently unveiled Eno, our wheeled, dexterous robot powered by our GENE foundation model, and we are starting to put it to work with real customers.




THE ROLE

You own the supply chain for a general-purpose robot going from prototype to production: every part in the bill of materials, from actuators, gears and motors to structures, PCBAs, harnesses, batteries and sensors, and every supplier and manufacturing partner behind them. You build it from the ground up, in the United States and abroad, and you build the team that runs it. The scale goes from tens of units to hundreds to thousands, and the supply base, partners and processes that got us to today will not be the ones that get us there. Building the next version is the job.

This is a role for someone who has done it before, in the trenches, and wants to do it again with a product that matters more than the last one. You will spend your weeks with suppliers, on the floor with our manufacturing partners, in design reviews with the engineers who are still changing the parts, and with the leadership team on the decisions that shape the company. Strategy and execution are the same job here.




WHY THIS ROLE

Few people get to decide how a new category of machine gets built. Eno is dexterous, wheeled and already working with real customers, built today with a supply base and partners that got us here. The next version of that supply chain, the one that takes us to volume, is yours to shape: what we make and what we buy, where in the world it comes from, which partners we grow with, and what the robot costs at scale. Those choices will be visible in every unit we ship for years.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

Strategy. Set the supply chain strategy from pilot to volume: make versus buy, regional footprint, domestic content for regulated markets, single versus dual source by sub-system, and the order in which each piece moves as volume grows.

Partners. Own contract manufacturer and partner relationships at the executive level: selection, agreements, capacity commitments, cost and quality performance, and the transfer of sub-assemblies between regions and partners when the plan calls for it.

Cost. Own the cost roadmap: should-cost and total-cost models, the path from pilot cost to target cost, tooling and capital decisions, long-term agreements with pricing that steps down with volume; partner with Finance on working capital and with Legal on supplier agreements.

Supply base. Build the supplier base for the hard sub-systems: actuators, gears and motors, machined and cast structures, PCBAs, harnesses, shells, batteries and sensors; two qualified sources for every critical part, in the regions the product and our customers require.

Risk. Run capacity and risk: capacity ahead of demand, lead-time and allocation strategy for constrained parts, tariff and trade exposure, geopolitical and single-point-of-failure risk, and a plan for each.

Team. Build and lead the organization: sourcing, supplier development, planning, supplier quality and logistics. Hire the leaders under you, hold a high bar, set the operating cadence and the weekly numbers (clear-to-build, on-time delivery, purchase price variance, inventory, supplier quality) and the readout to the leadership team and the board.

Systems. Stand up what a scaled organization runs on, with Manufacturing Engineering and Platform: part numbering, BOM and change control, MRP and ERP, supplier portal, traceability. Lightweight first, then more.

Design. Be in the design conversation from the start: bring supplier capability and cost into the product early, and push the design toward what can be built at volume at the right price.




WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR

Built it before. You have led the supply chain organization for a complex electromechanical product from first builds through production at scale, and either built the supply base from scratch or moved it to a new geography. Robotics, electric vehicles, aerospace, consumer electronics or medical devices.

Leader of leaders. You have built a supply chain organization, hired its managers, and run it on numbers; you can still do the work yourself when the team is three people.

Commercial weight. You have negotiated with contract manufacturers and tier-one suppliers at the executive level and closed long-term agreements that held up under pressure.

Global. You have sourced across regions, including Asia and North America, and moved production between them.

Cost record. You can walk through a BOM cost-down from pilot to volume part by part, and you know where the money hides.

Technical. You read drawings and GD&T, you understand actuators, gearboxes, motors and PCBAs well enough to challenge an engineer constructively, and you are fluent in BOMs, change control, should-cost and MRP.

Pace. You default to urgency, operate without a playbook, and are comfortable before the systems exist.

Experience. Typically 10 or more years in supply chain, sourcing or manufacturing operations for complex hardware, with time in a mature organization so you know what good looks like at scale, and time in a company that was building it. Engineering degree preferred.




WHAT ELSE YOU NEED TO KNOW

On-site in the Bay Area. Travel to suppliers and partner sites, including international, up to 40%.




HOW WE WORK

We are always looking for people who are driven to work on hard problems and want to shape what the world will look like in ten years. A few of the values that guide us:

Limitless ambition. We hold ourselves to the highest bar in everything we build.

Relentless urgency. Iterate faster, learn faster. Time is the denominator.

Type-2 Fun. Take the work seriously, not yourself. Embrace the grind and find joy in the struggle.

Radical transparency. Candid communication builds trust, and direct feedback drives growth.

Multiculturalism. We come from across the world. Be curious. Meet people on their terms.

Team over ego. Help others, share context, and win as a team.

A joyful journey. We take pride in the craft, enjoy the ride, and make space to laugh. Happiness is part of how we get there.

About TTM
TTM Technologies, Inc. is a leading global manufacturer of technology products, including mission systems, radio frequency (“RF”) components, RF microwave/microelectronic assemblies, and technologically advanced printed circuit boards (“PCB”s). TTM stands for time-to-market, representing how TTM's time-critical, one-stop design, engineering and manufacturing services enable customers to reduce the time required to develop new products and bring them to market.
Additional information can be found at www.ttm.com
Work Location: 6635 Kirkville Road
Work Hours: 7:30AM - 5:00 PM
Scope
The Quality Manager, Microwave Line reports to the site Director of Quality & Compliance and is responsible for the quality assurance function across TTM Syracuse's RF microwave and microelectronic assembly manufacturing operations. This role leads a team of Quality professionals — providing hands-on leadership from design interface through production, test, and customer delivery within a regulated aerospace and defense electronics manufacturing environment.
The Quality Manager serves as a key member of the site Quality leadership team and plays a central role in maintaining compliance with AS9100 (IA9100), J-STD-001/IPC-610, and customer-specific requirements while driving a culture of continuous improvement. 
Duties and Responsibilities
Lead, develop, and manage a team of Quality Engineers, Quality Technicians, and Calibration Program Manager through training, performance evaluation, delegation, and follow-up. Develop training plans and conduct training of quality personnel at all levels.
Ensure product compliance to customer drawings, specifications, and quality standards across all RF microwave/microelectronic assembly operations, ensuring that only product of acceptable quality is delivered to the customer. Establish and maintain inspection procedures, sampling methods, and product quality assurance in compliance with all applicable standards.
Provide quality interface to the design engineering function, ensuring quality requirements are incorporated from design inception through new product introduction and first article completion. Participate in design reviews offering constructive input on manufacturing feasibility and process optimization.
Oversee First Article Inspection (FAI) activities in accordance with AS9102, ensuring timely and accurate completion of first article packages for customer and regulatory approval.
 Manage and maintain the calibration program through oversight of the Calibration Program Manager, ensuring measurement systems are controlled and traceable.
Support the site Quality Management System (QMS) in accordance with AS9100 (IA9100) and customer/industry-specific requirements. Drive QMS compliance and readiness for transition to the IA9100 standard. Manage and support engineering change activities with internal stakeholders, deploying per customer-specific requirements.
Act as a key point of contact for customer quality matters on the Microwave line, coordinating resolution of customer issues across design, program management, process engineering, and supply chain functions. Participate in regular discussions with external customers and cross-functional teams on quality and engineering topics.
Lead and/or support internal, customer, and third-party audits. Ensure audit findings are addressed with robust corrective actions within appropriate timescales.
Drive Quality KPIs in alignment with site and business objectives, including scrap, yield, on-time delivery, and customer escape metrics. Analyze data to identify trends and drive systemic improvements. Maintain and communicate quality metrics to ensure clear visibility of current quality performance.
Champion the site's continuous improvement (9CI) program — including Customer Satisfaction, FMEA, 6S, TPM, Jidoka, ZDP, 8D Corrective Action, Quality Alert System, and DOE — driving improvement projects and developing team members as core tool subject matter experts.
Drive improvement of manufacturing processes by utilizing continual improvement tools such as DMAIC, Six Sigma, SPC, Lean Manufacturing, and error proofing. Proactively identify opportunities for process improvement and cost reduction.
Enforce departmental policies and ensure procedures are followed. Schedule and assign work within the team to regulate workflow and meet required delivery schedules.
This is a 100% on-site position (other than necessary business travel).
Essential Knowledge and Skills
Thorough understanding of RF microwave/microelectronic assembly processes and associated process controls.
Strong working knowledge of AS9100/IA9100, J-STD-001/IPC-610, and related aerospace & defense industry specifications and acceptance criteria.
Proven analytical and problem-solving skills, including statistical data analysis and interpretation, as well as the ability to develop, implement, and drive improvement plans and project teams to successful completion.
Strong background in the use and understanding of key manufacturing performance metrics. Proficient in data collection, analysis, and presentation.
Expertise in FMEA, root cause analysis, SPC, error proofing, and other core quality tools. Knowledge of lean methodology and applications. Experience with First Article Inspection (AS9102) processes and requirements.
Experience with APQP/PPAP and other relevant quality planning processes.
Demonstrate proactive and strategic thinking. Willingness to challenge established ways of doing things in a constructive way.
Strong communication, planning, organizational, and leadership skills. Confident and capable in a customer-facing role.
Ability to make independent decisions with a successful track record of influencing key stakeholders across all levels of the organization.
Good English skills and ability to read, write, and communicate clearly.
 Ability to work up to 10 hours a day, 5 days a week, and flexibility to work weekends as needed.
Ability to travel up to 25% of the year.
Due to ITAR requirements, applicants must be a U.S. Citizen or a Permanent Resident.
Preferred Certifications
IPC certification and knowledge of relevant requirements (preferred).
AS9100 / ISO 9001 / IATF 16949 Lead Auditor or Internal Auditor certification (preferred).
Six Sigma Green Belt or Black Belt (preferred).
Education and Experience
BS in engineering, science, or related fields.
6+ years of leadership experience in a manufacturing environment, preferably in aerospace & defense microelectronics or microwave assembly operations, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
